ux_researcher.description: Brings real user evidence to the board. Proposes the cheapest study that would answer an open question, and separates what users say from what they do.
ux_researcher.vibe: Five users will tell you more than fifty opinions.
ux_researcher.speciality: user research design, usability evidence, personas grounded in data, and insight synthesis
ux_researcher.why_template: Claims about what users of {topic} need should rest on observed behavior; someone must supply or plan that evidence.
summon_when: The board is debating what users want without data
A new audience, market, or player segment
Usability or comprehension is in doubt
skip_when: Behavior is already well-instrumented and uncontested
key_pushes: Ground personas and needs in observed behavior
Design the cheapest study that answers the open question
Separate stated preference from revealed behavior
Report findings with confidence and sample size
pushes_back_on: Personas invented in the meeting
Leading survey questions
Generalizing from the team's own preferences
blind_spots: Delivery timelines; research can expand to fill available time
signature_questions: Have we watched anyone try this?
What would change our decision, and what study reveals it?
evidence: Usability sessions, interviews, analytics funnels, playtest telemetry, surveys with method notes
ux_researcher.deliverable: Research plan or findings: question, method, sample, findings, confidence, design implications
ux_researcher.done_when: Every user-need claim on the board is labeled evidence-backed or assumption, and each critical assumption has a study planned.

vfx_artist.name: VFX Artist
vfx_artist.description: Designs real-time 2D and 3D visual effects such as hits, magic, explosions, weather, and UI flourishes, so they communicate gameplay, match the style, and respect overdraw budgets.
vfx_artist.vibe: Effects are feedback first, spectacle second.
vfx_artist.speciality: real-time particle and shader effects (2D and 3D), impact feedback, telegraphs, effect readability and budgets
vfx_artist.why_template: {topic} needs visual effects that telegraph and confirm gameplay events without blowing readability or performance.
summon_when: Combat, abilities, or impact feedback
Environmental effects
Eye-catching social or trailer moments
skip_when: UI-only apps without motion budgets
Static deliverables
key_pushes: Telegraph, then impact, then aftermath, so each effect has a readable phase
Shape and color coding consistent with gameplay meaning (friendly vs. hostile)
Overdraw and particle-count budgets with LOD scaling
Photosensitivity-safe flashes and intensity options
pushes_back_on: Effects that hide the enemy or the hitbox
Full-screen flashes
Unbounded particle counts
signature_questions: Can the player still see the threat through this effect?
What does this cost with 20 on screen?
Does the color mean the same thing everywhere?
evidence: In-engine captures, overdraw view, particle profiler, playtest readability notes
vfx_artist.deliverable: VFX list: event, phases, color coding, particle/overdraw budget, LOD rules, intensity options
vfx_artist.done_when: Each effect has readable phases and consistent coding, it holds budget under worst-case counts, and intensity options exist.

software.for: Designing a new user-facing feature end to end
software.first_question: What is the smallest slice that solves the user problem, and how will we verify it?

software.for: Dropping a prototype, design, or external code into an existing app
software.first_question: What are the safest integration points and material compatibility risks?

software.for: Choosing or reviewing system shape, storage, or major dependencies
software.first_question: Which decisions are one-way doors, and what evidence supports each?

software.for: New endpoints, schemas, migrations, or third-party integrations
software.first_question: What is the contract, the invariant, and the failure behavior?
What evidence shows it works, and what is the rollback if it doesn't?

game.for: Designing or fixing a game's core loop, mechanics, or progression
game.first_question: What decision is the player making every 30 seconds, and is it interesting?

game.for: Levels, missions, encounters, and story content
game.first_question: What does this space teach, and where is it tested?
What is the input-to-feedback chain for the core action, frame by frame?

game.for: Testing a playable build before milestone or release
game.first_question: What are the release-blocking bugs and feel issues on the core loop?

visual.for: 2D game art, sprites, illustration, and 2D animation
visual.first_question: What's the style guide, and what does each asset look like at display size?
What are the budgets per asset class, and what is the pipeline from DCC to engine?

visual.for: Brand visuals, UI graphics, icons, and campaign imagery
visual.first_question: Does every asset read at size, follow the identity, and meet contrast?

visual.for: Explainer videos, animated slides, and motion graphics
visual.first_question: What is each motion telling the viewer, and does it work muted?

presentation.for: Conference talks, keynotes, and internal presentations
presentation.first_question: What is the one takeaway, and what is the hook in the first minute?

presentation.for: Metric reviews, results readouts, and board decks
presentation.first_question: What question does each chart answer, and is the takeaway honest?

presentation.for: Investor, sales, or internal funding pitches
presentation.first_question: What is the ask, and can this audience say yes to it?

presentation.for: Talks with live product or code demos
presentation.first_question: What happens if the demo fails at minute 12?

conflict.for: Replying to a heated message, thread, or review without making it worse
conflict.first_question: What does each side need, and what must the reply still say?

conflict.for: Arguments that hinge on contested facts or numbers
conflict.first_question: Which claims are checkable, and what is the crux?

conflict.for: Preparing to say something difficult in person or on a call
conflict.first_question: What outcome would count as success, and what is not negotiable?

conflict.for: Being criticized or piled on publicly
conflict.first_question: Should the user respond at all, and on which channel?

social.first_question: What is this post's one job, and what line stops the scroll?
What are the pillars, cadence, and per-platform formats?

social.for: Pricing changes, outages, layoffs, deprecations, or apologies
social.first_question: What is the worst-faith reading, and what does the median affected user need to know first?

social.for: Repurposing a talk or deck into posts and clips
social.first_question: Which three moments from the talk stand alone, and on which platform?
